open_obligations: Note that Goel et al. study correctness grading, not choosing between debaters.
Check whether using distinct LLMs, as Liang et al. recommend, removes the similarity effect Goel et al. find across families.
Check the partial-correlation controls for accuracy.
in.other_title: LLM judges favour functionally similar models (affinity bias), average r = 0.84
in.rationale: Liang et al. state an LLM judge may prefer its own outputs and recommend same-LLM or distinct-LLM setups. Goel et al. report an average Pearson r = 0.84 between judge scores and judge-model similarity across 9 judges, extending beyond self- or family-preference; their judges grade free-text answers for correctness, not debate sides.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether LLM judges prefer outputs from themselves or similar models, for LLM-as-a-judge on MMLU-Pro

text: The authors state that MAD costs more time because agents interact over multiple rounds, that LLM agents may lose coherence and context in long debates, and that an LLM judge may prefer outputs generated by itself. To mitigate this bias they recommend that the judge and debaters all use the same LLM, or that the judge and debaters use distinct LLMs.
title: MAD limitations: time cost, long-context failures, judge self-preference
